text.p: BORN ON THIS DAY

King RICHARD II of England, the man credited with inventing the handkerchief, was born in 1367. - The French martyr JOAN OF ARC, who fought to drive the British from France, was born on this day in 1412.

English writer and feminist CAROLINE DEXTER was born in 1819. Her "Institute of Hygiene" in Melbourne promoted divided skirts and the abolition of corsets. British landscape artist HENRY LLOYD was born on this day in 1830. Most of his work was done in Australia, including the well-known painting "Hobart Town From The New Wharf".
American actor TOM MIX, noted as the most popular cowboy on the silent screen, was born in 1881.
American actress LORETTA YOUNG, who won an Oscar for "The Farmer's Daughter", was born in 1913.

One of the founders of the Australian hard rock band 'AC/DC' MALCOLM YOUNG was born in 1953. The guitarist was born in Glasgow but emigrated from Scotland in 1963. With his younger brother ANGUS, he formed 'AC/DC'in Sydney in 1973.
U.S. singer, harmonica player and song writer with the 'Fabulous Thunderbirds' KIM WILSON was born in 1951.
American pro-golfer NANCY LOPEZ-MELTON, was born in 1957.
U.S. singer KAHTY SLEDGE, youngest of the 'Sister Sledge', was born in 1959.
British bass player with 'Frankie Goes To Hollywood' MARK O'TOOLE was born in 1964.
EVENTS
1536 : The ex-wife of King HENRY VIII, CATHERINE of ARAGON whom he divorced, died today.
1540 : King HENRY VIII married his 4th wife ANNE of Cleves.
1838 : SAMUEL MORSE demonstrated his communications system using "dots" and "dashes" to send messages (in morse code) by telegraph over long distances.
1916 : The British Government brought in conscription, to secure more soldiers to replace the thousands killed in the trenches of France.
1919 : Former American President THEODORE ROOSEVELT, who began his career by running the New York Police and served in the White House from 1904-1909, died.
1928 : The River Thames broke its banks, drowning 4 people.
1930 : DON BRADMAN scored 452 not-out playing for New South Wales in the first innings of the match against Queensland.
1945 : The Allied forces overran 10 German tank divisions in winning the "Battle of the Bulge".
1969 : The US Presidential salary was doubled from $100,000 to $200,000.
1977 : Record company EMI dumped the punk-rock band "The Sex Pistols", claiming it couldn't handle continuing controversy generated by the group.
1981 : In New York MARK CHAPMAN pleaded insanity to the charge of murdering JOHN LENNON a month earlier.
1989 : RUPERT MURDOCH gained control of the British-based publisher WILLIAM COLLINS.
